learn.prompt: Two lamps are connected in parallel across a battery, each with its own switch. Which switches must be closed to illuminate ONLY Lamp 2?
learn.hint: Parallel branches are independent. Current flows through any branch whose switch is closed.
learn.explanation: In parallel, each branch connects directly across the battery terminals. Closing Switch 2 powers Lamp 2 independently of Lamp 1.

learn.prompt: You add a third identical resistor in parallel to an existing circuit. What happens to the total current drawn from the battery?
learn.hint: Adding another branch provides an additional path for charges to flow.
learn.explanation: Each parallel branch draws its own current V / R. Adding another branch provides a new path, increasing total current drawn from the battery.

misconceptionMap.b: In series, adding resistance decreases current. In parallel, adding a resistor adds another path, increasing total current.
misconceptionMap.c: The new branch draws current from the source, so the battery must supply more total charge per second.
misconceptionMap.d: A parallel branch does not short-circuit or stop existing branches.

learn.prompt: A 12 V battery powers two parallel branches: Branch 1 has 6 Ω and Branch 2 has 12 Ω. Set the total current leaving the battery.
learn.hint: Find the current in each branch (I1 = V/R1, I2 = V/R2), then add them together.
learn.explanation: I1 = 12 V / 6 Ω = 2 A. I2 = 12 V / 12 Ω = 1 A. Total current I = 2 A + 1 A = 3 A.

learn.prompt: Two 10 Ω resistors are wired in parallel. Enter their equivalent resistance in ohms.
learn.hint: For two identical resistors in parallel, Req = R / 2.

check.prompt: Why are household wall outlets wired in parallel rather than in series?
check.hint: Consider what happens when you unplug one appliance.
check.explanation: In parallel, each appliance receives the full 120 V/230 V line voltage and operates independently of other devices.

options.label: Each outlet sees the full line voltage and appliances run independently
Parallel wiring uses less copper wire than series
Appliances in parallel share current equally regardless of resistance
Parallel circuits prevent current from flowing

misconceptionMap.b: Parallel wiring actually requires separate runs to maintain independence.
misconceptionMap.c: Appliances draw current based on their own resistance: I = V / R.
misconceptionMap.d: Parallel circuits allow full operational current.

check.prompt: A 24 V source connects to an 8 Ω branch and a 24 Ω branch in parallel. Set the current flowing through ONLY the 8 Ω branch.
check.hint: Each parallel branch sees the full source voltage: I_branch = V / R_branch.

takeaway.title: Parallel branches are independent paths
takeaway.body: Every branch in parallel sees the full voltage. Branch currents add to the total, and equivalent resistance is always smaller than the smallest branch.
